blocks.text: The module documentation defines the conversation and replay streams, Redis key layout, encryption, rotation, TTL behavior, size budgets, and fail-closed policy. It then imports cryptographic and Redis-adapter dependencies without touching Redis at import time.
blocks.title: Ephemeral buffer contract and limits

blocks.text: _env_seconds accepts only bounded positive integer settings, so malformed or excessive TTL values fall back to defaults. Module constants establish record, request, item, stream, and read-page budgets.
blocks.title: Runtime TTL configuration

blocks.text: RedisLike defines the two commands the buffer needs, and _UpstashAdapter maps them to normal and transactional client calls. _call and _atomic normalize unexpected Redis failures into fixed BufferUnavailable errors.
blocks.title: Redis abstraction and fault conversion

blocks.text: Run ids and sequence numbers are constrained before Redis is touched. JSON serialization rejects non-objects, invalid numbers, and oversized payloads; replay messages must belong to this run and use an allowed event type.
blocks.title: Input and replay validation

blocks.text: _config validates current and previous secret settings without echoing them. _Box derives and caches per-key AES-GCM instances, binds records to run and stream associated data, and rejects malformed or unauthenticated wire data.
blocks.title: Configuration and authenticated sealing

blocks.anchor: def _seal_item(box: _Box, stream: str, kind: bytes, payload: bytes) -> list:
blocks.text: Items are split into framed encrypted records and grouped under the transaction budget. _read_stream authenticates every record, ignores duplicates, and emits only complete items in completion order.
blocks.title: Framing, chunking, and stream reads

blocks.text: TTL calculation limits idle refresh by the sealed hard cap and keeps a short-lived marker for expired buffers. _check verifies the sealed creation stamp and counters before callers refresh or mutate the buffer.
blocks.title: TTL and metadata integrity

blocks.text: The public functions create, inspect, refresh, delete, read, and append buffers. Sequence allocation is atomic, conversation writes validate JSON objects, and replay_after deduplicates events by sequence before returning them.
blocks.title: Public lifecycle, conversation, and replay API

blocks.anchor: def _append(run_id: str, stream: str, payloads: list) -> None:
blocks.text: _append checks the stream byte cap, seals and groups payloads, and delegates each group to _push. _push uses RPUSHX, refreshes all three TTLs, and increments the relevant byte counter in one atomic request.
blocks.title: Atomic append path

purpose: The module keeps run content in Redis only while a run is active, sealing each record with a run-derived AES-GCM key. It provides lifecycle, conversation, sequence, and replay operations with hard-cap expiry, idle refresh, size budgets, and fail-closed validation.
